english.title: Resist court officer executing process to re-possess
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[resisted]_
(B)_[intentionally obstructed]_

**(..SPECIFY NAME..), an officer of a court engaged in executing process issued by the

(C)_[High]_
(D)_[County]_

Court for the purpose of enforcing a judgement or order for the recovery of or delivery of possession of premises at **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 10(1) and (4) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
resisted/intentionally obstructed
an officer of the court engaged in executing process by High Court/County Court
to enforce judgement/order for recovery/delivery of possession of premises

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 10(2) and requirement as to the terms of the judgement or order necessary before section 10 offence committed.
(ii) "Officer of the court" as mentioned in powers of arrest includes any sheriff, deputy sheriff, bailiff or officer of a sheriff and any bailiff or other person who is an officer of the county court.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
